headline: Oil Spikes Toward $120 And Sends Global Markets Tumbling
summary: Global stock markets fell as oil prices surged toward $120 per barrel. The war with Iran raised fears of inflation, supply disruptions and global economic instability.
why: Crude oil is the benchmark input for fuel, transport and petrochemicals, so sharp price spikes feed into inflation and corporate costs. Equity markets tend to react quickly when energy prices jump.
why_moved: Oil prices surged toward $120 per barrel amid the war with Iran, raising fears of inflation and supply disruptions. Those fears pushed global stock markets lower.
